excerpts:
There is no standard family-wide pinout for 2N2222 components. Before determining the functions of the pins (emitter, base, collector), you must identify all information regarding the specific part

...

The correct pinout for a 2N2222 component can only be determined by taking into consideration the emitter, base, and collector configuration used by the manufacturer for a particular part number, case style, and manufacturer's illustrated view. A 2N2222 component is an NPN bipolar transistor; however, the definition of NPN only defines the functionality of the leads (emitter, base, collector), not the location of the leads on the manufacturer's physical case.

|Terminal |Electrical role |What it does not tell you |
| --- | --- | --- |
|Base, B |Controls collector-emitter current when driven relative to the emitter |The center lead or a universal pin number |
|Collector, C |Carries the controlled current from the load in a common low-side NPN switch |Which lead appears left or right in your viewing direction |
|Emitter, E |Provides the reference side of the base-emitter junction and usually returns toward the lower potential |That every 2N2222-marked package places it on pin 1 |

...

## How Do You Use a 2N2222 as a Low-Side Switch?

For common low-side switch circuits, the load will connect between the upstream positive voltage source and the collector, while the emitter must return to ground. To drive the base, the controller should apply current through a current-limiting resistor to the transistor. Home / Parts

2N3904 transistor: pinout, ratings, gain and substitutes

By Bulan Sarkar
The 2N3904 in TO-92 is E-B-C : hold it with the flat face toward you and the leads down, and the emitter is on the left. In SOT-23 (Nexperia's PMBT3904) pin 1 is the base, pin 2 the emitter and pin 3, the single lead on top, the collector.

...

Share Share on WhatsApp    Copy link

Pinout by package

 2N3904 TO-92 · Diotec 1=E 2=B 3=C
Flat face toward you, leads pointing down: E, B, C from left to right.

...

1 (TO-92 drawing with leads 1, 2, 3 and symbol: E (1), B (2), C (3))  2N3904 TO-92 · MCC 1=E 2=B 3=C
Flat face toward you, leads pointing down: pins 1, 2, 3 from left to right.
Source: Micro Commercial Components2N3904 NPN General Purpose Amplifier (TO-92), p. 1 (TO-92 outline numbered 1 2 3; 1 emitter, 2 base, 3 collector)  PMBT3904 SOT-23 · Nexperia 1=B 2=E

...

1 (Table 2, pinning: 1 base, 2 emitter, 3 collector) ; NexperiaPMBT3904 40 V, 200 mA NPN switching transistor, p. 2 (Table 4, marking code %1A)

Which one do you have?

A TO-92 printed 2N3904 is the through-hole part, and every maker checked here uses the same E-B-C order. A three-lead SMD part marked 1A (Nexperia adds a one-character site code in front) is the PMBT3904, the SOT-23 version, with pins numbered base, emitter, collector.
If the print is worn or the bag says only "NPN", a 2N3904 and a BC547 look the same and have opposite pin orders. Meter it, as described further down , before you solder it.

Absolute maximum ratings

The three datasheets agree on the voltages: 40 V collector to emitter, 60 V collector to base and 6 V emitter to base.

...

* Collector-emitter voltage VCEO | 40 V | 40 V | 40 V
* Collector-base voltage VCBO | 60 V | 60 V | 60 V

...

* Logic level shifting, pulse stretching and oscillators up to tens of megahertz.
Above 50 mA, use a PN2222A (same pins, rated 1 A) or a logic-level MOSFET. The 2N2222 page has its pinouts, and the trap in them.

Worked example: switching a 50 mA load

A 12 V load drawing 50 mA, say a relay whose coil measures 240 Ω, switched from a 5 V microcontroller pin. The emitter goes to ground, the coil sits between +12 V and the collector, and a resistor feeds the base from the pin.
1. Pick the base current. The datasheets specify saturation at 50 mA with 5 mA of base current, a ratio of ten: 50 mA / 10 =5 mA.

2N2222 NPN Transistor Pinout

2N2222 pinout for the modern TO-92 package, why it's usually a PN2222A underneath, and what changes on the older metal-can version.
2N2222 NPN Transistor Pinout Table of Contents
* Pinout (TO-92 package — what’s actually sold today)
* Why “2N2222” on a TO-92 part is a bit of a misnomer
* Identifying it on the breadboard

...

2 plastic package A generic 2N2222A NPN transistor, TO-92 package. Photo: MarkMossGH , CC0 (resized)

Pinout (TO-92 package — what’s actually sold today) #

Almost every 2N2222 sold on Amazon or from a hobbyist supplier today is in the small black plastic TO-92 package, and is electrically a PN2222A or 2N2222A underneath the “2N2222” printing — more on why that matters below. Holding the transistor with the flat face toward you and the three legs pointing down:
* Pin (left to right) | Name | What it does
* 1 | Emitter (E) | Current exits here in normal NPN operation
* 2 | Base (B) | The control pin — a small current here switches a much larger current through collector–emitter
* 3 | Collector (C) | Current enters here, from the load being switched
This E-B-C left-to-right order (flat face toward you) is confirmed on ON Semiconductor’s own PN2222A datasheet, and it’s the layout printed on the vast majority of TO-92 “2N2222” listings. It’s also the same order used by other extremely common TO-92 parts like the 2N3904 and BC547 — which is genuinely useful, since it means a lot of beginner circuits built around “a small NPN transistor”

...

The part that actually matters is remembering that the physical pinout identification method is different between the two packages — tab-relative on the metal can, flat-face-relative on the plastic

...

With the transistor’s flat side facing you and the three legs pointing down toward the breadboard, left to right is always Emitter, Base, Collector on a standard TO-92 2N2222/2N2222A/PN2222A.

...

The most common beginner use is switching a load — an LED, a small relay coil, a low-current motor — that a microcontroller pin can’t drive directly:
* Base resistor , typically 1kΩ–10kΩ, between the microcontroller output pin and the base. This limits base current to a safe level; skipping it is the fastest way to destroy the transistor, since the base-emitter junction behaves like a diode with very little built-in current limiting of its own.
* Load (LED, relay coil, motor) between the positive supply and the collector.
* Emitter tied to ground, shared with the microcontroller’s ground.

results.title: Transistor as Switch: NPN and PNP Circuit Explained - Zbotic
excerpts:
### NPN Transistor

- Structure: N-P-N semiconductor layers
- Symbol: Arrow on emitter points OUT (away from base)
- Switches ON when Base is HIGH (positive voltage relative to emitter)
- Current flows from Collector to Emitter when ON
- Load is connected between the positive supply and the Collector
- Common examples: BC547, BC548, 2N2222, 2N3904

### PNP Transistor

...

The NPN transistor switch is the most common configuration for Arduino projects. Here is how it works:

### Circuit Connection (NPN Low-Side Switch)

```
+VCC (e.g. 12V)
   |
 [LOAD] (e.g. relay coil, motor, LED strip)
   |
   C  (Collector)
   |
   B ----- [Rbase] ----- Arduino GPIO (HIGH = 5V)
   |
   E  (Emitter)
   |
  GND (common with Arduino GND)

```

**When Arduino GPIO is HIGH (5V):** Base-Emitter junction is forward-biased → transistor saturates → Collector-Emitter acts like a closed switch → current flows through the load → load is ON.

**When Arduino GPIO is LOW (0V):** No base current → transistor is cut off → Collector-Emitter acts like an open switch → no current through load → load is OFF.

...

Hardware: BC547 (NPN), 10kΩ base resistor, LED with 330Ω series resistor, breadboard, 5V Arduino Uno.

Connect: Arduino pin 9 → 10kΩ → BC547 Base. BC547 Collector → 330Ω → LED → +5V.

  delay(1000);
}


### Example 2: NPN Relay Switch with 2N2222

Hardware: 2N2222 (NPN), 1kΩ base resistor, 1N4007 flyback diode, 5V relay, 12V external power supply for relay, Arduino.

Connect: Arduino pin 8 → 1kΩ → 2N2222 Base. 2N2222 Collector → relay coil → +12V. 1N4007 across relay coil (cathode to +12V). 2N2222 Emitter → GND (common with Arduino GND).

```
// NPN relay switch with 2N2222
const int relayPin = 8;

void setup() {
  pinMode(relayPin, OUTPUT);
  digitalWrite(relayPin, LOW); // Relay OFF on start
}

void loop() {
  digitalWrite(relayPin, HIGH); // Relay ON
  delay(2000);
  digitalWrite(relayPin, LOW);  // Relay OFF
  delay(2000);
}

```

- **No common ground:** If your load is powered by a separate 12V supply, ensure the 12V GND is connected to the Arduino GND.

With the flat face of the TO-92 package facing you and legs pointing down — BC547 pin order is E-C-B (left to right), while 2N2222 (TO-92 metal can version) is E-B-C. The most common through-hole 2N2222A plastic TO-92 is E-B-C. Always check the datasheet for the exact part you have.
